parameters.content:
## Pinterest product pins
Writes a Pinterest pin for each product from its own data, a person approves it in Slack, and a paced queue posts it through Zernio so nothing goes out twice or in a burst. The image is always the real product photo: padded to 2:3 for the first pin, then placed in a fixed HTML frame with a headline, then with a customer review quote. No AI touches the image.

### How it works
1. **Setup** creates the `pins` and `pin_reviews` tables, adds one sample review and lists your Pinterest boards with their ids.
2. **Draft** (every morning, and after each Approve or Skip) keeps `max_waiting` pins waiting in Slack. It picks products that match a board, works out each product's next pin (`pin_sequence`), looks at the photo with a vision model for the alt text, writes the title and description for Pinterest search, checks them and posts a card.
3. **Frame** is the web page for framed pins. **Render** screenshots it with Firecrawl and keeps the JPEG in Shopify Files.
4. **Review** takes Slack's button clicks: Approve, Edit, Skip, Cancel.
5. **Book** gives an approved pin the next slot in your pace and schedules it in Zernio.
6. **Sync** (hourly) reads back what went live and updates the card.

### Setup
Credentials: Shopify (client ID and secret, `read_products`, `write_files`), Slack bot token and signing secret, Ollama, Firecrawl, Zernio (header `Authorization: Bearer ...`). Fill in each lane's settings, run Setup, put the board ids in **Draft settings**, publish, and set your Slack app's Request URL to **Slack button click**'s production URL. Full steps in the README.

### Customisation
Boards, search phrases and skip words are in **Draft settings**. Swap the sample review for your own reviews in `pin_reviews` (or your review app's API). To post with Pinterest's own API, replace **Schedule on Pinterest** and **Ask Zernio**.

## 1. Setup (run once)
Creates `pins` and `pin_reviews` (keeps existing ones), adds a sample review, and lists your Pinterest boards from Zernio so you can copy their ids into **Draft settings**.

## 2. Draft (every morning, and after each Approve or Skip)
Keeps up to `max_waiting` drafts in Slack, one pin per product at a time. Next pin in `pin_sequence` once the last one has been up `next_pin_after_days`. Vision model for the photo, chat model for the words, then the checks.

## 3. Card
One renderer for every state of a pin (draft, scheduled, posted, skipped, failed). Posts a new card or updates the existing one. Called by the other lanes.

## 4. Frame (web page)
The 1000 x 1500 page for headline and review pins, drawn from the saved row only. Open `?id=<pin id>` in a browser to design it.

## 5. Render
Firecrawl screenshots the frame page, wsrv.nl turns it into a JPEG, Shopify Files keeps it at a lasting URL for Slack and Zernio. A redrawn frame replaces the old file.

## 6. Review (Slack's Request URL)
Checks Slack's signature first. Approve books a slot (never a sample review), Edit opens a modal, Skip drops the pin (on a first pin, the whole product), Cancel takes a scheduled pin back to a draft.

## 7. Book
One slot after the last scheduled or posted pin: a week divided by `pace` for the account's age, jittered, inside posting hours. Only a draft or failed pin can be booked.

## 8. Sync (hourly)
Asks Zernio about pins whose slot has passed: posted with the pin link, or failed with Try again. One line per pin to the log channel.

### Posts to Pinterest
Creates a real scheduled pin in Zernio. Test with `first_slot_after` set weeks ahead, then Cancel.

### Writes to Shopify Files
Adds one image file per frame, and deletes the old one when a frame is redrawn.

parameters.query:
create table if not exists pins (
  id integer generated by default as identity primary key,
  product_id text,
  product_title text,
  handle text,
  pin_no integer,
  pin_kind text,
  board_key text,
  board_name text,
  board_id text,
  title text,
  description text,
  alt_text text,
  headline text,
  product_line text,
  review_quote text,
  review_rating integer,
  review_author text,
  review_source text,
  image_url text,
  source_image text,
  photo_kind text,
  shopify_file_id text,
  link text,
  problems text,
  status text,
  slack_channel text,
  slack_ts text,
  decided_by text,
  decided_at timestamptz,
  post_id text,
  scheduled_for timestamptz,
  posted_at timestamptz,
  pin_url text,
  error text,
  "createdAt" timestamptz not null default now(),
  "updatedAt" timestamptz not null default now()
);
create table if not exists pin_reviews (
  id integer generated by default as identity primary key,
  product_handle text,
  rating integer,
  quote text,
  author text,
  source text,
  verified boolean,
  "createdAt" timestamptz not null default now(),
  "updatedAt" timestamptz not null default now()
);
create unique index if not exists pins_product_image on pins (product_id, pin_kind, source_image);
create index if not exists pins_status on pins (status);
create index if not exists pin_reviews_handle on pin_reviews (product_handle);

parameters.text: Look at this product photo. Reply with JSON only: {"kind": one of "product" (the product on a plain background), "in_use" (installed or in a real setting), "packaging" (a retail box), "diagram" (dimensions, a spec sheet, mostly text), "other"; "alt": one plain sentence under 200 characters describing what is visible: the product type, its colour and shape, and the setting. No brand claims, no sales words.}

nodes.name: Write the pin

messageValues.message:
=You write Pinterest pins for {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.store_name }}, {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.store_description }}. You get one product. Reply with these lines and nothing else:
Pin title: the pin title
Description: the pin description
{{ $json.pin_kind === 'headline' ? 'Headline: the headline for the image\nProduct line: the product line for the image\n' : '' }}
Pin title rules:
- Start with the search phrase, or a close variant that fits this product. Then one key spec. Brand and model last.
- 40 to 90 characters. Never more than 100.
- Capitalise each word.
- If earlier pins are given, never repeat an earlier title.

Description rules:
- Five plain sentences including the closing line, about 450 characters in total, never over 500.
- Sentence one: what it is, with the search phrase, worded differently from the title.
- Sentence two: where it is used and who it suits. Use one of the other searches only if it reads naturally.
- Sentence three: three specs people search for, only if the product data has them.
- Sentence four: two more practical facts from the specs (setup, power, the app, what is in the box).
- End with: {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.closing_line }}
- Each search phrase at most once. No keyword lists, hashtags, emojis, links, phone numbers or prices.
{{ $json.pin_kind === 'headline' ? '\nHeadline rules:\n- A short benefit in plain words, at most 40 characters, from the product data only.\n- No price, no percentages, no claims the data does not support.\nProduct line rules:\n- Brand and model, then two key facts, separated by \" · \". At most 60 characters.\n' : '' }}
All lines:
- Write model numbers as given.
- Only facts in the product data. Never add a spec, a number or a feature, and never call it something it is not.
- Calm and factual. No fear and no hype.
- Never mention the image, photo or picture itself.
- Write in {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.language }}. {{ $('Draft settings').first().json.style_rules }}
- Never use the long dash character.

nodes.notes: One call per pin. Pin title, Description (and Headline, Product line for a headline pin).

nodes.notes: Safe fixes are made; everything else is a warning on the card.
